target_customer: Engineering organizations running more than 100 microservices (per the Nebula launch post); later positioned as AI data extraction for developers and enterprises
problem: Developers struggle to understand service dependencies and data flow across microservices. The YC page one liner instead describes an AI-powered data extraction engine.
business_model: B2B SaaS deployed in the customer's cloud
product_category: Developer tools, code navigation and data extraction

founders.name: Shanelle Roman
founders.background_notes: YC page: product manager at Google on a Google Ads buying experience.

founders.name: Vishnu Menon
previous_startups: Toucan AI (ML startup, outcome not checked)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post calls him a second-time founder.

competitors.name: Port
competitors.what: Internal developer portal with a software catalog dependency graph

technical_complexity.rationale: Indexing inter-service communication inside a customer's cloud and exposing it in an IDE extension, catalog and GraphQL API needed real distributed systems work from two people.

defensibility.rationale: Deep deployment in customer clouds could create some lock-in, but service catalog vendors could add dependency views and no proprietary data is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Service catalog tools were adding dependency features around 2022 to 2023; no source shows any of them acting on Indexical.

market_need_then: The Nebula launch post cites a Statista figure that 85% of enterprises use microservices and says growing complexity slows delivery, debugging and onboarding.

rebrands.why: not stated; YC lists the launch post under Nebula and the company page under Indexical

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand; searches returned unrelated Nebula companies.

outcome_analysis: The cause of Indexical's inactive status is not public. The company launched as Nebula, a microservice dependency navigation tool, and the YC page now describes AI data extraction, but no source dates or explains that shift. Funding appears small, about $125K to $500K by aggregators, and no shutdown or acquisition news was found, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Both rounds rest on single aggregators: VCBacked lists a $500K pre-seed in April 2023 for a YC backed Nebula that may or may not be this company, and Dealroom lists a $125K seed with an undated, garbled total. The company website field is empty so no site was fetched. Whether the shift from Nebula to data extraction was a pivot is not sourced, so pivots is empty. Toucan AI outcome not researched.
